body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"siainbuletin"} -->
_Requested by **Sia** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2ApjJf3fNB4nmVud6MqNpBi)_

Stacked on #16 (base is its branch); merge #16 first and GitHub will retarget this one to `main`.

**Before:** every box in the browser graph and the SVG export had the same colour, and a click on a box folded it. The page only knew the part of the tree that Emacs had cut, so it could not move to another note.

**After:** `vulpea-hierarchy-tag-colors` maps a file tag to a colour (defaults for `root`, `idea`, `question`, `claim`, `evidence`, `source`). A note takes the colour of the first of its tags that is listed, drawn as a tint, and the legend lists the tags in view. In the browser, a click on a box recentres the graph on it and remakes the nodes from there. A small ▾ marker folds a branch, `−` and `+` change the depth, and `←` or Backspace goes back to the previous centre. The SVG export uses the same colours.

**How:** the page now embeds the whole tree and runs the depth cut itself (the same breadth-first walk as `vulpea-hierarchy--scope`), so recentring needs no Emacs round trip. For a very large vault this makes the page bigger, since it holds every note of the hierarchy (ids, titles, tags and paths). Tested on mock notes in headless Chromium: tint colours, legend, a recentre, a depth change, back, and a JavaScript syntax check; `dot` accepts the tinted Graphviz source. Not run against your real vault. The literate doc is regenerated and tangles back byte for byte.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01YKB9W9Svzsc4PYxBD8qL9Q)_

comment_data.body:
Confirmed: in headless Chromium the marker's computed `pointer-events` was `none` and its font 14px. Fixed in 22292b8 with a `.node text.fold` rule after `.node text`; the marker now reports `all` and 12px. The fix is merged up the stack (#18, #19, #20).

commit.message:
Tint boxes by file tag and recentre the browser graph on click

vulpea-hierarchy-tag-colors maps a file tag to a colour. The browser page
now holds the whole tree and cuts the part to show itself, so a click on a
box recentres on it; a fold marker, depth buttons and Backspace are added.
The SVG export uses the same colours. The literate doc is regenerated.

commit.message:
Cut the tree in Emacs to the levels the browser page holds

The page no longer embeds the whole vault. vulpea-hierarchy-embed-depth
(4) limits the levels below the starting note, a larger depth you ask
for wins, and notes at the edge show how many children were left out.

commit.message:
Make the fold marker clickable

The rule .node text turned pointer-events off for every text in a box,
including the fold marker, and was more specific than .fold. A click on
the marker recentred the graph instead of folding. The marker now has
its own rule after it.
